headline: Penguins' Ben Kindel hospitalized after medical emergency on flight
take:
ESPN reports that Penguins forward Ben Kindel was being evaluated at a Salt Lake City hospital Tuesday after a medical emergency on the team's flight home from a four-game trip. No further details have been given.

Our numbers can't say much about his health, but they show what he has been worth on the ice. So far this season, Kindel has two goals and two assists in nine games, averaging 17.32 minutes. His own expected goals, a measure of the quality of the chances he's taken, sit at 2.45, so he is slightly below that with two goals. At 5-on-5, PIT has taken 49.06 percent of the expected goals with him on the ice, and the team's share is 4.77 points better when he sits, a small sample. PIT is 3-6-1 with 47.9 percent of the expected goals overall, so the team has been outplayed more often than not. Kindel was a regular contributor last season (17 goals, 35 points in 77 games), and his absence, however long, would remove a significant piece of the lineup.
